title: Router and WAN
description: Is the hEX router healthy, is the WAN link up and how fast, how are the lab VLANs loaded, and how close is the ISP quota? Open it after RouterCpuHigh, RouterHot, RouterWanLinkDown or a WAN quota alert, and on the weekly review to read the quota pace.

panels.title: Is the router and its uplink OK?
WAN link (ether1)
panels.description: Link state of ether1, the cable to the Biznet router (rule RouterWanLinkDown: ifOperStatus is not up for 1 minute). DOWN means the whole lab has no internet. Check the cable and the Biznet router; physical, so the operator.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Average load of the hEX's 4 cores (rule RouterCpuHigh: above 85 % for 10 minutes). Normal is a few percent (a 24-hour average of about 2 %, peaks near 8 %). High means a scan hitting the firewall, a log flood or SNMP walks; the per-core chart below shows if one core is pinned.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Share of the hEX's 256 MB of RAM in use (rule RouterMemoryHigh: above 90 % for 15 minutes). Normal is about 25 %. Rising without recovering is a leak or a huge connection table; reboot in a quiet moment after a snapshot.

targets.expr: 100 * hrStorageUsed{job="snmp_hex", hrStorageDescr="main memory"} / hrStorageSize{job="snmp_hex", hrStorageDescr="main memory"}

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: Board temperature of the hEX (rule RouterHot: above 70 C for 15 minutes; the raw MikroTik value is tenths of a degree, divided by 10 here). Normal is low 40s. High is airflow: physical, so the operator.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the hEX last booted (rule RouterRebooted, info: fires under 10 minutes). The hEX has no battery, so a short uptime is usually a power cut; HostOnBattery at the same time confirms it. Red only for the first 10 minutes.

panels.title: Inbound peak, 24 h
panels.description: Highest 5-minute average of WAN inbound traffic in the last 24 hours. This is the throttle indicator: once the 1500 GB monthly quota is gone the ISP caps the line at about 5 Mbit/s and the peak sits flat at 4.9 Mbit/s (red, below 5.5). A free line peaks above 10 Mbit/s on a normal day. Heuristic: a truly idle day also reads low. No alert rule watches it, and WanInboundDayHigh cannot fire while throttled (5 Mbit/s moves at most about 53 GB a day).

panels.title: WAN inbound, 24 h
panels.description: Bytes received on ether1 in the last 24 hours (rule WanInboundDayHigh: above 60 GB for 1 hour). The plan allows about 50 GB a day on average. Red means something is pulling hard right now: run services/kubeletto/tenant-bandwidth.sh.

panels.title: WAN inbound, 7 days
panels.description: Bytes received on ether1 in the last 7 days (rule WanQuotaPaceHigh: above 350 GB for 1 hour, the pace that uses up the 1500 GB plan before the renewal on the 16th). Same expression as the Overview tile.

panels.title: Router health: CPU, memory, temperature, power
CPU per core
panels.description: Utilisation of each of the 4 cores. The dashed line is the 85 % that RouterCpuHigh uses, but that rule averages the cores for 10 minutes, so one pinned core with three idle ones does not fire it. RouterOS exposes no run-queue or load average over SNMP, so saturation is not visible here.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Share of the 256 MB of RAM in use. The dashed line is the 90 % of rule RouterMemoryHigh (15 minutes). A staircase that never comes back down is a leak. Absolute usage is about 62 MiB.

targets.expr: 100 * hrStorageUsed{job="snmp_hex", hrStorageDescr="main memory"} / hrStorageSize{job="snmp_hex", hrStorageDescr="main memory"}

panels.title: Board temperature
panels.description: Board temperature in degrees C (tenths in SNMP, divided by 10). The dashed line is the 70 C of rule RouterHot (15 minutes). The hEX has no fan, so it follows the room: a daily swing is normal, a climb toward 70 is airflow.

panels.title: Supply voltage
panels.description: DC input voltage of the hEX (tenths of a volt in SNMP, divided by 10). A flat line near 12 V is a healthy adapter. Dips or drift point at the power brick or a brown-out. No alert rule watches it.

panels.title: Uptime and reboots
panels.description: Days since boot, over 7 days. Each drop to zero is a reboot (rule RouterRebooted, info: under 10 minutes). The hEX has no battery, so a drop with no change window is usually a power cut.

panels.title: Device errors and memory allocation failures
panels.description: The errors leg of USE for the router: hrDeviceErrors on the CPU cores and failed memory allocations, per second. Both stay at 0 on a healthy hEX; any line above 0 means the router is out of resources. No alert rule watches it.

panels.title: Link state: WAN and trunk
panels.description: Link state of ether1 (WAN, rule RouterWanLinkDown) and ether5 (the trunk to the switch: if it is down, every VLAN is cut off from the router). ether2 to ether4 are spare or out-of-band and normally down, so they are not shown.

panels.title: WAN throughput
panels.description: Bit rate on ether1, in and out. The port is 100 Mbit/s and the plan is 100 Mbps, but after the monthly quota the ISP caps the line at about 5 Mbit/s: the dashed orange line marks that ceiling, and inbound that flattens against it is the throttle. Inbound is what the quota counts. The router exposes no per-flow counters, so who is pulling comes from the tenant-bandwidth script.

panels.title: WAN errors and discards
panels.description: Packets per second the WAN port counted as errors (bad frames: cable, port, duplex) or discards (dropped for lack of buffer or by policy). Healthy is 0 on every line. Errors that grow point at the cable or the Biznet router port. No alert rule watches it.

panels.title: Negotiated link speed
panels.description: Speed each port negotiated: ether1 should read 100 (the Biznet router's port) and ether5 1000. A drop to 10 or 100 on ether5 is a bad cable or port and throttles the whole lab; a drop on ether1 caps the WAN below the plan. No alert rule watches it.

panels.title: ISP quota (1500 GB a month, throttled to about 5 Mbit/s after)
WAN inbound, rolling 24 h
panels.description: Bytes received on ether1 in the trailing 24 hours, over 7 days. The dashed line is the 60 GB of rule WanInboundDayHigh (1 hour); the plan averages 50 GB a day. Once the line is throttled it cannot move more than about 53 GB a day, so this rule goes quiet after the quota is gone: read the throttle indicator instead.

panels.title: WAN inbound, rolling 7 days
panels.description: Bytes received on ether1 in the trailing 7 days, over 30 days (the retention). The dashed line is the 350 GB of rule WanQuotaPaceHigh (1 hour): a week above it is on pace to use up the 1500 GB plan before the renewal on the 16th. Prometheus keeps 30 days, so this is a pace, not the billing-month balance; the real remaining quota is in the Biznet portal.

panels.title: WAN inbound rate and peak (throttle ceiling)
panels.description: Inbound bit rate on ether1 and its highest 5-minute average over the trailing hour, over 7 days. The dashed orange line is the ISP's 5 Mbit/s throttle. A peak that runs flat just under it (4.9 Mbit/s) for hours is the throttle; a free line shows peaks of 10 to 60 Mbit/s. Feeds the 'Inbound peak, 24 h' tile.

targets.legendFormat: inbound, peak of the trailing hour

panels.title: k3s-worker inbound (TenantWorkerInboundSustained)
panels.description: Bit rate received on the Kubeletto tenant worker's eth0 (rule TenantWorkerInboundSustained: the 30-minute average above 2.5 Mbit/s for 2 hours, about 27 GB a day). The worker takes nearly all of the WAN inbound, so this is the early pointer to who is eating the quota; eth0 can also carry lab-internal traffic. Above the dashed line: run services/kubeletto/tenant-bandwidth.sh to name the tenant.

panels.title: Lab VLANs: load per router interface
VLAN traffic into the router (from the hosts)
panels.description: Bit rate arriving at the router from each VLAN's hosts: 10 MGMT, 20 SERVERS, 25 DMZ (k3s), 30 LAB, 40 TRUSTED, 50 IOT/GUEST (pick VLANs with the filter at the top). The trunk is 1 Gbit/s, so anything near 1 Gbit/s is saturation. The router has no per-flow counters, so this says which VLAN, not which host.

panels.title: VLAN traffic out of the router (to the hosts)
panels.description: Bit rate the router sends into each VLAN. The DMZ (25) carries the Kubeletto tenants, so most of the WAN inbound reappears here. An idle VLAN (30, 40, 50) sits near 0.

panels.title: VLAN volume, last 24 h (in plus out)
panels.description: Total bytes through each VLAN interface in the last 24 hours, both directions, largest first. Use it to rank which VLAN is busy; the line charts above show when.
